claims.claim: **Hyperkalaemia = K over 5.5 mmol/L** (normal 3.5–5.0), **or over 6.0 mmol/L in neonates.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Severity (mmol/L):** **severe >7.0** · moderate 6.1–7.0 · mild 5.5–6.0.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Hyperkalaemia that is moderate or severe risks arrest and life-threatening arrhythmias: get an ECG and begin cardiac monitoring. Stop any potassium-raising medications or fluids.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Confirm with a second sample** (collection artefact, e.g. a haemolysed sample, is a listed cause) — ⚠️ **but if the level is critically high and the scenario fits, treat before the repeat result.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **ECG changes:** peaked T waves (early), prolonged PR, flattened or lost P waves, widened QRS, bradyarrhythmia and blocks; **severe: sine wave, ventricular arrhythmia, PEA, asystole.** ⚠️ **A normal ECG does not exclude arrhythmia risk.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Other tests:** UEC, glucose, venous gas, ± urine electrolytes; CK, cortisol/aldosterone (especially with hyponatraemia) or digoxin level as the cause suggests.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Calcium gluconate 10%: 0.15 mmol/kg (0.68 mL/kg), max 6.6 mmol (30 mL), slow IV/IO — over 15–20 minutes when stable, 2–5 minutes when unstable.** Preferred with only a peripheral line.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Calcium chloride 10%: 0.14 mmol/kg (0.2 mL/kg), max 6.8 mmol (10 mL), slow IV/IO — over 15–20 minutes when stable, 2–5 minutes when unstable.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Stop if the heart rate drops significantly; watch for extravasation. Never give with bicarbonate; do not give in digoxin toxicity.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Onset under 3 minutes, lasts about 30 minutes.** The ECG should normalise; if not, repeat the dose (twice) or give an infusion titrated to response.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Nebulised salbutamol:** 25 kg or less 2.5 mg; over 25 kg 5 mg (max 10–20 mg), **repeated every 1–2 hours.** Onset 30 minutes, lasts 2–3 hours.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **IV salbutamol only if severe and after discussion with a senior clinician**; monitor for tachycardia.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Severe: IV bolus of glucose 10% at 5 mL/kg (if not hyponatraemic) plus an IV bolus of short-acting insulin, 0.1 unit/kg (max 10 units)**, followed by an insulin/glucose infusion.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Moderate: glucose 10% with 0.9% sodium chloride at maintenance rate plus short-acting insulin infusion 0.1 unit/kg/hour IV.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **High risk of insulin error: dilute 10 units (0.1 mL) to 10 mL with 0.9% sodium chloride (1 unit/mL) and draw the dose from that. Check glucose every 30–60 minutes.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Sodium bicarbonate — metabolic acidosis only.** Severe hyperkalaemia with acidosis: 8.4% at 1–3 mL/kg (= 1–3 mmol/kg), IV over 5 minutes. Mild–moderate with acidosis: 1 mL/kg (= 1 mmol/kg) given slowly IV over 30 minutes. ⚠️ **Not with calcium.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Polystyrene sulfonate resin 0.5–1 g/kg (max 30 g) 6-hourly PR or oral (with lactulose)** — mild effect, multiple doses needed. Separate from other oral medicines by at least 3 hours.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not use resins with ileus, recent abdominal surgery, perforation or hypernatraemia.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Dialysis:** organise with the paediatric renal or intensive care team and transfer to a tertiary centre.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Involve the paediatric team for all moderate or severe hyperkalaemia**, or an underlying cause such as renal abnormality. **Seek specialist advice if there is renal disease or complex co-morbidity.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider transfer for all severe hyperkalaemia and anyone needing dialysis.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge** when potassium is normal and stable, the child is asymptomatic with a normal ECG, and the cause is treated.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23
